subject: Using INLA for jointly modeling of three responses

messages.author: 9feb199ac47dd68b
messages.subject: Using INLA for jointly modeling of three responses
parts: I am new to application of INLA. I am working on a project with three responses that I need to model jointly.  I have done the unstructured and spatially structured components for each of these responses without joint modeling and things have run well. I now want to model them jointly and I don't how to go about it in INLA. Can someone shed light on how to go about this or referral to any material that can be helpful?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Using INLA for jointly modeling of three responses
parts:
Hi Moses,

what kind of response variable likelihood models do you have?
Depending on what they are, and depending on what latent model component are joint between the three models (or how you want to join them) it may be easier to first rewrite the models as inlabru models (inlabru.org), since it will then be easier to turn it into a joint model. There are currently more examples on how to build joint models that take advantage of the "copy" feature in ordinary INLA, but for three responses that can become quite messy in comparison with how an equivalent model can be setup with inlabru (inlabru handles most of the complex spatial setup internally before handing it over to inla() for the actual calculations; it means you don't have to setup you own inla.stack() calls, for example.
With some more details on the model definitions I may be able to be more specific.

Finn
